stem:
Arjun built the loop shown below on his desk: one cell, a lamp, an ammeter, and a variable resistor. He now wants a circuit diagram of the same loop using standard symbols.

Which statement about that diagram is correct?

options.text: The lamp may be drawn as any neat sketch of a torch bulb, because a circuit diagram is just a tidy picture of the parts.
Each part must use its standard symbol: the cell as a long line and a short line, the lamp as a circle with a cross, and the ammeter as a circle marked A.
The cell should be drawn with two separate lamp branches leaving it, so both the lamp and the ammeter get their own loop.
The long and short lines of the cell may be drawn either way round, because the direction of the cell does not matter in a diagram.

teacher.key_rationale: A circuit diagram uses standard symbols, not a sketch of the real parts. The source figure already shows those symbols for cell, lamp, ammeter and variable resistor.
